universe.name: Experiment Eve
universe.tagline: The shortest night of the year. The longest night of her life.
universe.setting: Kingsport, the Quiet Isle — an unnamed coastal country, Sunday June 21, 1998, 8:00 PM to 5:11 AM
universe.logline: An escapee of the Experiment crosses a collapsing city in one real-time night to reach a place called Providence, carrying an unsigned Father's Day card.

entities.name: Katie 'Kat' Weiss
entities.summary: Protagonist. Escapee of the original outbreak zone; rode the Colony Line freight into Kingsport at exactly 8:00 PM and found the city going the same way. Trying to reach Providence by dawn.

details.namedFor: Critical Path (1993), starring Eileen Weisinger as Kat
details.carries: One pistol clip and an unsigned Father's Day card she has had for three weeks
details.voice: Dry, oblique, never explains what she knows. First line: 'What a shit hole.'
details.knowledge: Clearly knows what the Experiment was. Never says it.

entities.name: The Observer
entities.summary: Unknown watcher on the other side of the CCTV lenses. Proves their existence by intervening: electric locks buzz open a beat before an ambush, lights snap on over the safe path, payphones ring as Kat passes.

details.reading: A father figure — watching over her, or checking up on her. Never resolved in dialog.
details.channels: Analog CCTV (some with warped fisheye lenses), payphones, ApertureOS machines (future)

entities.name: SOAK
entities.summary: Graffiti artist, one half of the dueling-tag war across Kingsport. Father of REN. His stencil diagrams double as weapon blueprints (the flamethrower). Argues municipal history in paint: 'THEY TAKE THEM TO THE ISLAND.'

entities.name: REN
entities.summary: Graffiti artist, son of SOAK. Crosses out his father's pieces; answers in red. 'the island was FIRST.' The tag war is a family argument conducted across a dead city.

entities.name: The Pawnbroker
entities.summary: North End pawnshop owner. Trades equipment only for baubles — pocket watches, pearls, rings, silverware. Pays in bullets and doesn't meet your eyes. Pays double for the Blue Dress and asks nothing. Shop signs: 'CLOSED SUNDAYS' and 'BACK IN 5' — both lying differently.

entities.name: M.
entities.summary: Co-owner of North-End Salvage. Left notes for Ray: keep the bay lamp lit — 'people walk toward light, that's all we can do now.' Deleted from the office computer: 'The boys made you something. It is on your bench. Come home and get it.'

entities.name: Ray
entities.summary: Tow driver at North-End Salvage. Took the flatbed to the Bell Bridge approach on June 21 and did not bring it back. A construction-paper Father's Day card with two crayon hands is still waiting on his workbench.

entities.name: The Erasure Team
entities.summary: Hazmat-suited cleanup squads burying the outbreak. Shoot on sight. Run the operation from the Island. Not chimeras — that is the point. Often caught off guard: coffee at a barrel, peeing off the bridge approach. Somebody's dads: kill one and a kid's crayon drawing falls out of his helmet.

details.combat: Rifle with a laser-sight telegraph; weak point is the air tank on the back — flank them.
details.stealth: View-cone + noise detection; an undetected approach on an off-guard trooper allows an Execution — a free kill before the fight starts.

entities.name: The Chimera Ecology
entities.summary: Every monster is a chimera — two everyday animals fused; the grafted anatomy carries the attack telegraph. Species behave as rival factions: they free-wander, hunt in packs, fight each other to the death or morale break, eat what they kill, and GROW (juvenile → adult → giant). Nests spawn juveniles. Monstrous parenthood is the design key.

entities.name: Frog Chimera
entities.summary: Bloated frog + insectoid bulb-tipped tongue (the tongue is like a certain plumber-adjacent dinosaur's). Body shots deal a flat 1. The bulb — targetable only while the tongue is extended — takes massive damage; time the battle pause to the tongue. Telegraph: it inflates and its jaw drops.

entities.name: Crow-Spider
entities.summary: Spider + fluttering crow wings. THE WING-FLUTTER IS THE TELEGRAPH: wings rise and beat, then a ballistic leap. Flaming variants crawl out of the burning semi. The giant one is not a species — it is one that ate well.

entities.name: Rat-Gull
entities.summary: Plump rat + stubby gull wings. Skittish scavenger of the rail yards; flees people, eats street rats, grows. Wing-flare telegraph, hopping lunge, periodic glowing eye.

entities.name: Trashclaw
entities.summary: Raccoon + lobster. Armored frontally (flat 1 damage) until its claw slam whiffs — dodge the slam and it overbalances, exposing the soft ringed tail.

entities.name: Steeple Bat
entities.summary: Bat + moray eel head. Roosts under the Bell Bridge and on fire escapes. Sonar-chirp telegraph (maw glows) then a dive; wound it mid-dive and it crash-lands into a helpless crawl.

entities.name: Shellback
entities.summary: Harbor seal + snapping turtle. A living roadblock: retracts fully invulnerable, then the neck lunges out on a horrible stretch — the neck is the weak point, mid-lunge only.

entities.name: Stilt Stag
entities.summary: Deer + heron. A tall fog-walker on stilt legs; rears its head high, then the beak plunges to street level and sticks — punish the stuck head; kneecapping it brings everything lower.

entities.name: Quillspray
entities.summary: Skunk + porcupine. Rears up (belly exposed — the window) before a frontal gas-and-quill volley.

entities.name: Tentacled Doberman
entities.summary: Doberman + squid tentacles rooted along the spine. Fast pack rusher; tentacles coil (glowing) before the lash — shoot the coil to stagger it. Setpiece packs slam the chain-link fences they can never cross.

entities.name: Gutter Serpent
entities.summary: House cat head + centipede body. Slinks in a weave; segments regrow — only killing the cat head ends it. Hiss telegraph with flattening ears.

entities.name: Sting Gull
entities.summary: Seagull + jellyfish bell. Drifts over fences trailing tendrils — a slow floating hazard that periodically swells, glows, and dips. Fragile; pops.

entities.name: Scythe Mare
entities.summary: Carriage horse + mantis forearms. Rears with arms unfolded and wing-cases popping open (the weak point) before either a full charge or a 180-degree scythe sweep.

entities.name: Bloat Sow
entities.summary: Pig + engorged tick abdomen. Feeds on corpses and visibly swells. Explodes on death — killing it NEXT TO its friends is the tactic the game never explains.

entities.name: Hush Fox
entities.summary: Red fox + great horned owl. Dead silent, hunts camera blind spots — but shows plainly on CCTV zones (the Observer's lenses). The only warning is the eye-glint.

entities.name: Drain Coil
entities.summary: Garter snake + lamprey mouth. Buried at sewer grates; erupts, latches, and drains — hit the exposed mouth-ring to break the latch, then punish the writhe.

entities.name: Cobble Crab
entities.summary: Green crab + barnacle-rubble armor. Camouflages as barricade debris (forts tie-in); unfolds with hinging plates and popping eyestalks. Sometimes flips itself — the underside is everything.

entities.name: Dart Squirrel
entities.summary: Gray squirrel + paper wasp. Tiny, fast, erratic; hovers with blurring wings then darts straight through you. Comes in tree-nest swarms; burn the nest or thin the pack.

entities.name: Lure Heron
entities.summary: Great blue heron + anglerfish esca. Dangles a glowing lure that MIMICS an item sparkle — the game's fake pickups. Shooting the lure itself is the crit; enough lure damage dims it forever and slows the snap.

entities.name: Hive Bear
entities.summary: Black bear + paper-wasp hive grown through the torso. Boss. Body shots ANGER the hive (wasp clouds sting you for trying); the roar splits its chest open — the hive core is the only sane target. It is protecting its children.

entities.name: Bulwark Moose
entities.summary: Bull moose + snapping-turtle shell plating. Siege engine: frontal armor (flat 1), hoof-scrape telegraph, a 12-meter charge that SMASHES fort walls and changes the map — and ends with its antlers stuck. The stuck window is the fight.

entities.name: The Afflicted
entities.summary: The human chimeras — the zombie tier. Not survival of the fittest: wild clashes of a person and a creature that should never share a body. Clumsy but unpredictable; they shamble in lurches and FALL DOWN unexpectedly, mid-anything (helpless a moment, twice as vulnerable, then the scramble up). They were people. Their names are what the neighbors called them.

entities.name: Flailfish
entities.summary: A man's legs; a huge fish for an upper body that never stops flailing. Sprints in bursts, then the fish slaps a half-circle. Weak point: the gasping mouth.

entities.name: Crabwife
entities.summary: A woman with crab claws far too heavy for her arms — they drag on the pavement. She heaves one up, visibly struggling, and the crushing pinch spins her clean around. Weak point: her exhausted face.

entities.name: Gullscream
entities.summary: A man whose head is a full-size gull mid-scream. Wanders confused, then a rapid peck flurry. The open throat is always a target — a mercy.

entities.name: Mothmother
entities.summary: A woman with giant moth wings that drag behind her. A labored wing-heave, a blinding dust burst, and then she just stands there, spent. Drawn to any light left on.

entities.name: Houndfather
entities.summary: A man with a hound's forelegs where arms should be, running on all fours with a gait that is WRONG. Pounces, overshoots. Still wears the collar. Weak point: the collar.

entities.name: Eelneck
entities.summary: A man whose neck is a meter of eel. The head strikes on its own while the body stumbles past, oblivious.

entities.name: Owlneighbor
entities.summary: His head turns all the way around and never stops facing you, however his body wanders. The blink before the grab is enormous.

entities.name: Pigeonchest
entities.summary: A man whose ribcage is a roost. He grips his own ribs and the flock bursts out — then straggles home, one by one, while the hollow chest stands open.

entities.name: The Bride (Mantisbride)
entities.summary: A woman in a wedding dress with mantis forearms folded in prayer. She does not chase. The fastest strike in the tier, and every third one she stops to smooth her dress. Weak point: the bouquet she still holds.

entities.name: Shell-Boy (Snailson)
entities.summary: A young man carrying a snail shell grown through his back. Slowest of them all; teeters, then a crushing unstoppable roll that always ends with him on the ground.

entities.name: Backwards Pete (Serpentwaist)
entities.summary: Snake from the waist down, fused facing backward. He slithers away from you to attack you, head wrenched over his shoulder. Weak point: the twisted spine junction.

entities.name: Stilts (Gantrylegs)
entities.summary: A woman on three-meter heron legs; every step a near-fall. Folds down like a collapsing tripod to bite, and sticks there.

entities.name: Barnacle Dad
entities.summary: Crusted shut, arms sealed to his sides. All he can do is flop at you, and the flop always ends with him down. One barnacle over his heart glows.

entities.name: The Choir (Ratchoir)
entities.summary: A person whose lower half dissolved into a knot of rats that carries the exhausted torso around in skitter-bursts. Sometimes the knot unspools in a ring.

entities.name: Anglerwidow
entities.summary: Her lure bobs on a stalk and glows exactly like a save lamp across a dark street. The cruelest fake in the game. Shoot the lure and she gets frantic.

entities.name: Togglecrab
entities.summary: He can only move sideways, and flips sides without warning. His head strains to face you and never can. The body-check comes lean-first.

entities.name: Jellyuncle
entities.summary: A man whose skull is a jellyfish bell. Standing near him hurts. The whole man is the telegraph.

entities.name: Woodpeckerclerk
entities.summary: Work tie, woodpecker bill. He grabs, and then he DRUMS. Dizzy afterward, bill drooping.

entities.name: Tortoise Nana
entities.summary: An old woman in a floral shell, nearly invulnerable hunkered down — until the neck-snap bite, which is shockingly fast.

entities.name: Carpsire
entities.summary: The inverse of the Flailfish: a fish's tail for legs and a man's proud upper body, bathrobe intact. He advances by beaching himself, flop by flop. It was his bathtub, probably.

entities.name: Lockpicking (Real-Time)
entities.summary: A famous lockpicking minigame, borrowed shamelessly — rotate the bobby pin, feel for the sweet spot, torque, snap — with one change that changes everything: the world does not pause. She picks locks in real time with the street alive behind her, and a hit mid-pick snaps the pin. Locks only ever guard optional loot, never the route.

entities.name: Kingsport
entities.summary: The City by the Sea (design ref: Newport, RI — in-game names are all nods/winks; the city takes its name from the local author's own invented coastal town; his epitaph reads I AM PROVIDENCE). Act One of the campaign.

entities.name: Providence
entities.summary: The destination. A place friendly NPCs allude to as safe from the Experiment. The city up the Bay, the word for paternal care, and the epitaph — never disambiguated. Kat must reach it by dawn (5:11 AM).

entities.name: The Quiet Isle
entities.summary: The island holding Kingsport, Midway, and Northgate (design ref: Aquidneck — 'isle of peace'). Three towns, three acts, heading north to the bridges and up the Bay.

entities.name: Midway
entities.summary: The middle town (design ref: Middletown). Act Two.

entities.name: Northgate
entities.summary: The north town, the way off the island (design ref: Portsmouth). Act Three.

entities.name: Jacobstown
entities.summary: The island across the Bell Bridge (design ref: Jamestown/Conanicut; James → Jacob, same root).

entities.name: The Bell Bridge
entities.summary: The great suspension bridge over the Bay (design ref: Pell Bridge — one letter, and this game chimes the hours). Its approach is blocked by a jackknifed, burning semi in the slice; its eventual failure forces the Providence Belle arc.

entities.name: The Island (the old Asylum)
entities.summary: Design ref: Coasters Harbor Island. Built 1819 as the city asylum and poor farm — where the city sent the people it couldn't explain. Sold to the government in 1880; war was taught in it after 1884. Now Erasure runs the Experiment's cleanup from it. Boats leave full and come back empty. For 180 years this island is where the city sends what it can't explain — and it's had practice. Nobody says this aloud.

entities.name: The North End
entities.summary: Kingsport's neighborhood by the Colony Line rails — the vertical slice. Tracks, row streets, a searchable house, the CCTV cross street, the frog street, the burning-semi blockade under the bridge approach, chain-link corridors, and the salvage garage with the lighthouse lamp.

entities.name: Billy Island
entities.summary: Harbor island with the Harbor Light — the lighthouse save nearest the slice (design ref: Goat Island). The Lodge on it is the Erasure checkpoint civilians were told was a shelter.

entities.name: Thorn Island Light
entities.summary: Lighthouse save (design ref: Rose Island).

entities.name: Ottertail Light
entities.summary: Lighthouse save at Jacobstown's southern tip (design ref: Beavertail).

entities.name: Peach Beach Light
entities.summary: Lighthouse save in the Bay (design ref: Plum Beach).

entities.name: Low Country Light
entities.summary: Lighthouse save (design ref: Dutch Island).

entities.name: The Keeper's Rock
entities.summary: Harbor lighthouse save (design ref: Ida Lewis / Lime Rock — named for the heroine keeper).

entities.name: The Point Light
entities.summary: Lighthouse save at the end of the Drive, by the Inn on the Point (design ref: Castle Hill). Sunset chairs still aimed at the view; the guest book stops mid-signature.

entities.name: Fort Addams
entities.summary: The old harbor fort and festival grounds (design ref: Fort Adams; one added letter — the family would approve). An abandoned stage reads JUNE 20 BENEFIT — CANCELLED. Survivor stronghold vs. a wall-breaching Bulwark Moose; festival rigging is salvage heaven.

entities.name: The Swells
entities.summary: The grandest of the Summer Houses on Beauview Avenue (design ref: The Breakers — the waves, and the people who owned it). The bauble economy's endgame; Erasure evacuated the Avenue FIRST, and the placards downtown noticed.

entities.name: The Casino
entities.summary: Historic grass-court club (design ref: the Newport Casino / Tennis Hall of Fame). Floodlit courts, HALL OF FAME OPEN banners for a July that won't come; 13 courts, 13 camera zones.

entities.name: The Driftwood Library
entities.summary: The old subscription library (design ref: Redwood Library). Public-internet terminal with a PRINTED DIRECTORY OF WEBSITES; a librarian survivor who files everything, including what happened.

entities.name: Stella Maris College
entities.summary: The college in the mansions (design ref: Salve Regina — one Marian hymn swapped for another). Dorms in gilded guest wings; summer session meant somebody was home.

entities.name: The Wharfs
entities.summary: Harbor district. Boats leave for the Island all night and come back empty. Mo's Clam Shack (EST. 1931; the fryer is still warm), the Lobster Co-op (a Trashclaw nest, of course), Two Scoops (FATHER'S DAY SUNDAE — DADS EAT FREE), Colony Tea & Coffee at war with the new MoonDollars.

entities.name: Hotel Norseman
entities.summary: Gilded Age hotel (design ref: Hotel Viking, 1926). Rooftop view of half the map; room keys are ACTUAL metal keys — floor-by-floor gating with zero padlock puzzles.

entities.name: The Drive
entities.summary: Ten miles of open coast road (design ref: Ocean Drive). The bicycle showcase: pack chases, wind, dead cars with trunk tools. Ends at the Point Light.

entities.name: The Cliff Walk
entities.summary: 3.5 miles of coastal path between the Summer Houses and open sea. Fog, Sting Gulls over the rail, Shellbacks on the rocks. Fixed cameras were invented for this.

entities.name: First Beach
entities.summary: The family beach (design ref: Easton's). Snack bar, arcade with a Mega 64 demo kiosk, Shellbacks owning the sand, a carousel that runs all night on its own.

entities.name: The Out Island
entities.summary: The day-trip island people swear the Experiment never reached (design ref: Block Island). A ferry schedule with every departure crossed out but one. Sequel bait.

entities.name: The Colony Line
entities.summary: The freight railway along the Quiet Isle's west shore (design ref: Old Colony & Newport Railway). Kat rides it in and bails at 8:00 PM sharp; the train does not stop.

entities.name: MEGAHIT VIDEO
entities.summary: The video store (design ref: Blockbuster). NEW RELEASE: SINKING SHIP. The return slot is jammed with tapes; every one of them is Sinking Ship. BE KIND — REWIND. Nobody was kind.

entities.name: North-End Salvage
entities.summary: M. and Ray's garage on the truck route. Chain-link yard corridors behind it; inside, a salvaged lighthouse lamp sweeping the bay doors and an ApertureOS 98 machine that still has power. The slice's save point — and Ray's unclaimed Father's Day card.

entities.name: The Providence Belle
entities.summary: A 1928 motor yacht at the Wharfs (design ref: the classic harbor-tour yacht). The only way up the Bay to Providence once the Bell Bridge fails. Fueling and crewing her is the late-game arc. Her name was always a wink.

entities.name: ApertureOS 98
entities.summary: The fictitious 1998 operating system (a clear allusion to a certain window-themed OS) running on every save-point computer. Teal desktop, Commence button, SAVE.EXE, PERKS.EXE, MY DOCUMENTS, TRASH with UNDELETE — the juicy lore is always in the trash. SOLITAIRE.EXE is missing HEARTS.DLL. Everything is missing its hearts lately.

entities.name: The Unsigned Father's Day Card
entities.summary: Kat has carried it for three weeks. It isn't sealed. She hasn't signed it. Not for sale — the one bauble the pawnbroker will never be offered. Why she's really going to Providence, in card form. What she does with it at Providence is the endgame beat.

entities.name: The Blue Dress
entities.summary: Found hanging in the first closet she searches. 'I don't think it's my size... and what is that STAIN?!' Navy blue. Dry-clean only. It has been through something historic. The pawnbroker pays double and asks nothing.

entities.name: The Experiment
entities.summary: The thing that went wrong. Everyone in-world knows what it was, so no one explains it — not Kat, not the NPCs, not the signage. It arrives only in fragments: 'since the Experiment,' 'we are not your control group,' 'our kids drank it too.'

entities.name: The Collapse
entities.summary: The civil breakdown in the Experiment's wake. Society didn't fall to the monsters; it fell apart arguing about what had been done to it. Protests, cover-ups, forts of unclear authorship, tag wars, looted pawnshops.

entities.name: The June 20th March
entities.summary: CITY HALL TO THE PIER. BRING EVERYONE. IT IS OUR WATER TOO. The night before the game, whole swaths of marchers simply dropped where they stood — placards still in hand, no bullet wounds. Kat: 'I don't see any bullet wounds.' Their signs tell the rest.
Every stopped pocket watch in the city reads 6:47. They all stopped at 6:47. Which day, and why, is never stated.

entities.name: The Night (June 21, 1998)
entities.summary: Summer Solstice, Father's Day, a Sunday. Kat arrives by train at exactly 8:00 PM; sunset 8:23; sunrise — the deadline — 5:11 AM. The clock runs in real time and the City Hall bell counts every hour while the world holds still: WHAT A HORRIBLE NIGHT TO HAVE A CURSE.

entities.name: No Exposition Dumps
entities.summary: Everyone already knows what the Experiment was, so nobody explains it. Kat knows and never says. Lore arrives via item descriptions, graffiti, placards, deleted files, and offhand clues only.

entities.name: Placeless, Wink-Named
entities.summary: Never the real state or country; no real place or business names. Every name is a nod with the influence visible (see the gazetteer). Providence stays — that IS the wink.

entities.name: 1998 Technology Only
entities.summary: Landlines, pagers, fax lines, caller-ID boxes, dial-up that dies when the phone is picked up, VHS, paper maps from gas stations, floppy disks, Y2K preppers eighteen months early. Nothing newer exists.

entities.name: Nostalgia Bait, Trademark-Scrubbed
entities.summary: 1998 saturates everything but no real trademark is ever named: Sinking Ship, Finestein, Durpy, MEGAHIT VIDEO, AmeriGate Online, FreeNaught, Saga of Zelna, PocketBeasts, Bean Buddies, Pocket Pals, Mega 64, MoonDollars, Doorway 2000. Comedy is dark but ludicrous — Maniac Mansion tone.

entities.name: Father's Day Is the Through-Line
entities.summary: June 21, 1998 was Father's Day, and the whole night refracts fatherhood: Providence means paternal care; Kat's unsigned card; the Observer as watchful father; SOAK and REN; nests as monstrous parenthood; troopers who are somebody's dads; cold grills plated for cookouts nobody ate. Never stated. Only accumulated.

entities.name: Routing Is the Puzzle
entities.summary: Light puzzles, no fetch quests, no arbitrary combination locks. Blockers are diegetic (fire, collapse, a pack too big) and exploration is rewarded with the way around. Surviving the journey is the game.

entities.name: The World Is at War With Itself
entities.summary: STALKER-style A-Life scaled down: species wander, hunt in packs, fight rival factions to death or morale break, eat their kills and grow; nests restock the streets; Erasure fights everything. The player is one more participant, and letting factions bleed each other first is always a valid plan.
